origin.en: Mino, Gifu Prefecture, Japan (kilns at Ōgaya, Mutabora, Kamashita and Kujiri Motoyashiki)

summary.en: A thick, white, semi-translucent glaze of feldspar alone, the first white glaze of Japan, often over iron painting that shows through as soft brown.

safety.en: No colorant; feldspar dust holds free silica: mix it wet and wear a respirator for dry powder.

note.en: Feldspar alone (長石単味). Fukushima feldspar stands in for a Mino feldspar until a Kamado (釜戸) data sheet is found.

sources.citation: Kotobank, 志野焼 (Daijisen, Nihon Kokugo Daijiten, Nipponica, Mypedia, Britannica, Yamakawa).
吉田博和, 尾上彩, 常世田茂, 佐藤剛「笠間焼の新素地・新釉薬の開発」, 茨城県工業技術センター研究報告 第43号 (2014), Table 6.

gaps: No source for the firing (long reduction firing around cone 9–10 is unverified).
No Mino (釜戸) feldspar data sheet; Fukushima feldspar stands in.
